high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Applies Special Credit Mechanism for 18 Projects by Vingroup, Sun Group, and Masterise: A Strategic Adaptation of the Banking System?
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued a special credit mechanism for 18 key development projects belonging to Vingroup, Sun Group, and Masterise, with total capital requirements exceeding VND 752,000 billion (~USD 29.5 billion). Under this policy, outstanding loans extended to these projects will be **excluded from banks' annual credit growth quota (room tín dụng) calculations**, effectively creating a form of targeted credit room expansion. Participating banks can fund these projects without consuming their existing annual credit allocations.

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of June 25 at MB, HDBank, Sacombank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary: A survey of online deposit rate boards as of June 25, 2026 reveals continued bifurcation across Vietnamese bank tiers. Saigonbank leads the market at **7.2% p.a. for 12-month deposits**, while MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB all post **7.0% p.a.** for the same tenor — making five institutions now at or above the 7% threshold for 12-month terms. BVBank, LPBank, Bac A Bank, and OCB cluster just below at **6.9% p.a.**, with LPBank offering 6.95% for 18-month deposits. The state-owned Big 4 (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) have held their rates unchanged for several months, maintaining their notably lower positioning relative to private peers.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Issues Urgent Warning to All Citizens on Foreign Currency Trading
high.summary:
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) — specifically its Region 1 Branch — has issued an urgent public advisory warning citizens and businesses about the increasingly complex circulation of counterfeit foreign currency in the domestic market. The SBV is directing all FX cash transactions to be conducted exclusively through licensed commercial banks, foreign bank branches, or SBV-certified foreign exchange agents. Citizens are explicitly prohibited from buying, selling, or exchanging foreign currency cash between private individuals or through unlicensed entities.

The SBV emphasizes that unauthorized FX transactions carry dual risks: exposure to counterfeit currency causing direct financial losses, and legal liability under Vietnamese law (Article 27 of the relevant regulatory framework). This advisory signals continued SBV vigilance over informal FX channels, which can distort official VND/USD market dynamics and complicate reserve management. For FX traders, this reinforces the SBV's ongoing effort to tighten control over parallel/black market FX activity — a structural factor that, if left unchecked, could add upward pressure on the unofficial USD/VND rate. Watch for any follow-up enforcement actions or tightening of FX licensing regulations.

medium.title: A Banking Stock Backed by 32 Funds Simultaneously Amid Market Volatility
medium.summary: Vietnamese investment funds recorded significant net outflows in May 2026, with total net redemptions exceeding VND 2,500 billion — up 59.4% month-on-month, according to FiinGroup data. Equity funds bore the brunt, with net outflows of over VND 1,800 billion, a staggering 6.8x increase versus April and representing 71.6% of total market outflows. Notably, this marks the **31st consecutive month** of net redemptions from equity funds, with cumulative outflows reaching VND 69,400 billion — a structurally significant and persistent trend that signals sustained domestic retail investor risk aversion. Bond funds saw some relief, with net outflows declining 44.7% MoM to ~VND 742 billion, though this still represents the **9th straight month** of net redemptions (cumulative: VND 13,200 billion). ETF outflows surged 159% MoM to nearly VND 1,200 billion. Against this backdrop, 32 funds reportedly maintained or increased positions in one specific banking stock, suggesting selective institutional conviction even amid broad defensive repositioning. **For VN-Index watchers**, the persistent and accelerating fund outflow trend is a bearish structural signal for Vietnamese equities and warrants close monitoring of liquidity conditions heading into Q3 2026.

medium.title: Bank Profits Up 30–50x Over the Past Decade: The Fastest-Growing Banks Revealed
medium.summary: A review of Vietnamese bank financial statements from 2015–2025 highlights remarkable profit growth trajectories, predominantly among mid-sized private banks rather than state-owned institutions. **SeABank** leads the sector with a ~59x profit increase over the decade (from VND 117 billion in 2015 to VND 6,868 billion in 2025), implying a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of ~50%. **MSB** ranks second with a 46% CAGR (~45x growth, reaching VND 7,058 billion in 2025), while **LPBank** ranks third, growing from VND 422 billion to VND 14,269 billion. For international fund managers, this data underscores the long-term re-rating potential of Vietnamese private banking franchises. However, the context of persistent fund outflows (see above) and recent market volatility suggests near-term caution is warranted, even as the structural earnings growth story remains compelling for medium-to-long-term positioning in Vietnamese bank equities.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on June 24 at MB, HDBank, Sacombank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank...
medium.summary:
A survey of online deposit rates across major Vietnamese banks as of June 24 shows continued clear bifurcation in the market. Saigonbank leads the market at **7.2% p.a. for 12-month deposits**, followed by MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB at **7.0% p.a.**, while the majority of banks are clustered in the **6.5–6.9% p.a. range** for the same tenor. State-owned commercial banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) remain at the lower end of this range, maintaining a structural gap versus private and smaller banks. This rate environment suggests deposit competition remains active, particularly among mid-tier and smaller lenders seeking to build funding buffers — a dynamic that could become more acute if the SBV's special credit mechanism (Article 1) triggers increased disbursement demand. Bond investors should note that elevated deposit rates at the 6.5–7.2% range continue to offer competition to short-to-medium duration government bond yields.

medium.title: Latest Forecasts After SJC Gold Bar and Ring Gold Prices Drop More Than VND 15 Million per Tael
medium.summary: SJC gold bar prices closed at VND 143.2 million/tael (buy) and VND 146.2 million/tael (sell) on June 25, down VND 800,000 from the prior session and off more than **VND 15 million/tael** over the past month — the lowest level since late 2025. The decline tracks a sharp global sell-off, with international gold falling below **USD 3,997/oz**, breaching key support levels at USD 4,100 and USD 4,000, and now more than USD 1,600/oz below the historic high of USD 5,600+ set earlier this year. Physical demand was muted, with SJC outlets reportedly sold out of gold bars while limiting ring-gold purchases to three taels per customer.

medium.title: Gold Falls 28% from Peak — Experts Weigh In on Long-Term Outlook
medium.summary: Gold spot prices fell over 3% intraday to $3,980.20/oz, struggling to hold the key $4,000/oz support level, as the US Dollar Index surged to its highest level in over a year. The sell-off is being driven by strengthening Fed hawkishness, with CME FedWatch markets now pricing in rate hikes as early as September, with potential further tightening in December. For Vietnam-focused investors, a stronger USD and rising US rates carry direct implications: (1) **VND depreciation pressure** intensifies as the USD strengthens globally, potentially forcing SBV to intervene or tighten domestic liquidity; (2) capital outflow risks from emerging markets, including Vietnam, increase in a higher-for-longer US rate environment; and (3) domestic gold market volatility may affect consumer sentiment and informal USD/VND demand. Paul Williams of Solomon Global advises investors to view the current correction in context of longer-term structural gold demand, but near-term USD strength remains the dominant headwind. Watch for SBV's response to any sustained VND weakness in coming sessions.

medium.title: Fuel Prices Continue to Fall — Diesel Down Nearly VND 1,700/Litre
medium.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry and Trade conducted a scheduled fuel price adjustment effective 15:00 on June 25, 2026, resulting in broad-based price decreases. E5RON92 petrol fell VND 767/litre to a ceiling of VND 19,359/litre; E10RON95-III dropped VND 837/litre to VND 19,916/litre. Diesel (0.05S) saw the sharpest cut at VND 1,668/litre, now capped at VND 21,866/litre. Fuel price stabilisation fund contributions were set at VND 300/litre for bio-ethanol blends and VND 800/litre for diesel and mazut. For macro and FX traders, continued fuel price deflation is a **disinflationary input** that reduces headline CPI pressure, giving the SBV greater policy flexibility to maintain accommodative rates without stoking inflation — a mild positive for the bond market and VND stability management.

medium.title: VietBank (VBB) Share Surges Over 11% on Morning Session of June 26
medium.summary: VietBank's (VBB) stock surged more than 11% to VND 13,900/share during the morning session on June 26, extending a ~18% gain since the start of June and a remarkable 58% rally from its mid-March trough. The catalyst is a combination of a stock dividend (10% bonus share issuance with record date June 29) and HOSE's formal approval to list over 1 billion VBB shares, with the stock set to cease trading on UPCoM from June 30. The migration to HOSE is expected to significantly improve liquidity and attract both domestic and international institutional investors. This development is relevant as a marker of incremental capital market deepening in Vietnam's banking sector, with potential implications for foreign portfolio flows into Vietnamese bank equities.

medium.title: Banks Announce New Regulations on Transfers Exceeding VND 10 Million
medium.summary: ABBank has updated its corporate banking platform (ABBank Business) with enhanced biometric authentication requirements for digital transfers. New corporate clients (accounts or businesses under 12 months old) must have their legal representative provide facial recognition approval for transactions of VND 50 million or more per transaction, or VND 100 million cumulative daily. For businesses using simplified accounting under a single-approver model, facial authentication is required for transactions as low as VND 10 million per transaction or VND 20 million per day. This move reflects the broader regulatory push by the SBV to strengthen digital banking security and AML/KYC compliance across the Vietnamese banking system — an ongoing structural reform relevant to banking sector risk assessment.
